t: 3515 – Shortest Path in a Weighted Tree
o: Since the graph is a tree rooted at 1, the shortest path from root to x is simply the sum of edge weights on the root-to-x path. An edge-weight update (u,v,w′) shifts the depth of EVERY node in the subtree hanging below that edge by (w′ − w_old). Root the tree, record Euler-tour entry/exit times so each subtree is a contiguous range, and use a Binary Indexed Tree supporting range-add / point-query: update = add delta over [tin[child], tout[child]], query = prefix sum at tin[x]. Map each undirected edge to its child endpoint via parent pointers. Complexity O((n+q) log n), required for n,q up to 1e5.
k: Tree distances = root-path sums; an edge update shifts a whole subtree by a constant.
Euler tour turns subtrees into ranges → BIT with range-add/point-query.
Identify the child endpoint of an updated edge using parent pointers.

a.n: Approach 1: Euler Tour + Fenwick Tree (range add, point query)
a.i: DFS from root records tin/tout and each node's edge weight to its parent. Updating edge (u,v) finds the child c and adds delta = w′−wt[c] over c's subtree range; querying node x reads the BIT prefix at tin[x].
s: Root the tree iteratively; compute tin, tout, parent, wt[].
Update [1,u,v,w′]: locate child c, range-add delta over [tin[c], tout[c]].
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — DFS is O(n); each BIT operation is O(log n).

w: Recognizing 'tree + path sum + edge updates' → Euler tour + BIT is the interview takeaway. Pitfalls: iterative DFS to avoid recursion limits; identify the child endpoint correctly; distances fit in 64 bits (1e5 × 1e4). Follow-up: path queries between arbitrary nodes (add LCA with binary lifting), or HLD for general path updates.
